text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe shifts electoral debate toward labour measures, vows to widen scope of cuts in labour charges.
-- Subscriber TV channel Canal Plus reaches a broadcasting and production agreement with independent French film producers.
-- Regional newspaper L'Est Republicain buys majority stake in Les Dernieres Nouvelles d'Alsace.
-- Labour Minister Jacques Barrot says in an interview labour flexibility is not the main issue in the fight against unemployment, seeks wider cuts in labour charges.
-- Gaumont film producer makes a hit with French Luc Besson's film "Le Cinquieme Element", Gaumont shares rose 5.2 percent Friday.

-- Planned merger between Dassault and Aerospatiale may be jeopardised if the left wins the upcoming parliamentary election, since the project includes privatisation of Aerospatiale. Alliances between suitors in privatisation of Thomson-CSF may also lead to a partial dismantling of Aerospatiale.
-- Insurer GAN to try to sell real-estate assets.
-- French banks to launch new charge cards which check with a client's bank before each transaction, thanks to lower telecommunications costs.

-- SOFRES poll carried out for Le Figaro on May 9-10 finds centre-right ruling coalition winning 338-370 seats at the upcoming parliamentary election, and the left (including communists) falling below 200 seats.
-- FNAC bookstore chain seeks to negotiate further price cuts with publishers.
